# R SCRIPT TO PLOT SFS VALUES FOR EACH POPULATION
```{r}
basedir="/Users/erincollins/Google Drive/My Drive/Erin's Projects/chipps_angsd/angsd_results/"

# FALL pop plots
sfs_fall1996_2000<-scan(paste0(basedir, "/results/fall1996_2000.folded.sfs"))
barplot(sfs_fall1996_2000)
# mask the bin corresponding to a frequecy of 0 or 1
barplot(sfs_fall1996_2000[c(-1, -length(sfs_fall1996_2000))])

sfs_fall2001_2005<-scan(paste0(basedir, "/results/fall2001_2005.folded.sfs"))
barplot(sfs_fall2001_2005)
# mask the bin corresponding to a frequecy of 0 or 1
barplot(sfs_fall2001_2005[c(-1, -length(sfs_fall2001_2005))])

sfs_fall2006_2010<-scan(paste0(basedir, "/results/fall2006_2010.folded.sfs"))
barplot(sfs_fall2006_2010)
# mask the bin corresponding to a frequecy of 0 or 1
barplot(sfs_fall2006_2010[c(-1, -length(sfs_fall2006_2010))])

sfs_fall2011_2015<-scan(paste0(basedir, "angsd_sfs_fall2011_2015.folded.sfs"))
barplot(sfs_fall2011_2015)
# mask the bin corresponding to a frequecy of 0 or 1
barplot(sfs_fall2011_2015[c(-1, -length(sfs_fall2011_2015))])

sfs_fall2016_2018<-scan(paste0(basedir, "/results/fall2016_2018.folded.sfs"))
barplot(sfs_fall2016_2018)
# mask the bin corresponding to a frequecy of 0 or 1
barplot(sfs_fall2016_2018[c(-1, -length(sfs_fall2016_2018))])
```
